content.question_text: How do you access or change elements in an ArrayList?

core_requirements: Use the .get(index) method to access an element.
Use the .set(index, element) method to change/replace an element.
acceptable_variations: ArrayList uses get() for retrieval and set() for modification.

content.question_text: How does the add() method differ from the set() method in ArrayList?

core_requirements: add() is used to insert a new element (increases the size of the list).
set() is used to replace an existing element at a specified index (does not change the size).
You cannot use set() on an index that doesn't already have an element.
acceptable_variations: set() updates an existing element, add() adds a new one.

content.question_text: How can you get the flexibility of dynamic growth combined with convenient array-style element access?

core_requirements: Create an ArrayList and populate it with elements.
Then call the .toArray() method to copy the elements into a regular array.
This gives you the best of both worlds: flexible growth during population and fast indexed access afterwards.
acceptable_variations: Use ArrayList for building, then convert to array with toArray().
Populate ArrayList, then copy to array for faster access.

content.question_text: How do you add an element at a specific position (middle) of an ArrayList?

core_requirements: It inserts the element at the specified index and shifts subsequent elements to the right.
acceptable_variations: add(index, element) inserts at a given position.
Call add() with an index argument.

content.question_text: How do you remove an element from an ArrayList?

core_requirements: It can remove by index (remove(index)) or by object reference (remove(Object o)).
acceptable_variations: Call remove() on the ArrayList instance.
